text: A big worker survey said blood pressure fell 11 points, but only for people who cut back on salt.
Coffee seemed to give sleep-deprived students a small memory lift on one word test.
Remote work sped up three startups' software teams, though the benefit disappeared within half a year.
Buses crossing the new bridge saved riders around twenty minutes on average, versus the roadworks year.
Vitamin D might ward off colds, though only kids under five showed it in one supplement-funded winter study.
A reading app aided young English learners, but those benefits had worn off by the following school year.
Pesticide exposure in one season left bumblebee colonies with about a quarter fewer queens.
Icelandic public offices tried a four-day week: burnout fell, pay stayed the same, sick days didn't change.
